chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Playing for Father Divine's meetings
summary: He describes opening Father Divine's meetings with hot songs and hymns while hired preachers did the preaching.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: All we'd do was open up his set, you know, and play a few songs for him, you know, and get the people coming in, you know. Meeting them, spare a few hymns and let them come on in singing the hymns. That's all we did --
Yeah, we played them. We played anything to make some money, man. Things were rough. Yeah, boy. Yeah, I remember those days, man. We played a whole summer
up there. Then we went to Savoy in New York and played a couple of nights up Savoy.
What went on in Father Divine's meetings?

Well, you'd open it up. You'd heat them up with a couple of hot songs. And he'd come out there. You know, he didn't do much himself because he had these guys to preach for him, you know. He had -- he'd go hire the best preachers. These guys down South, man -- pay them good money. He didn't say much. He'd just sit back there and had two pretty girls fan him with the big fans, you know, and he's collecting the money, you know. He had buckets of money, man.
And he didn't do his own preaching? I didn't realize that.

No. Once in a while he'd say a few things but mostly he hired preachers, you know. He'd come out and say a few words, probably the closing words or something. He didn't no hard, no heavy preaching, no. We'd play a couple of nights for him, you know, kind of straight for a while.
That would have been what, about '29 or --
That was about '29, yeah, because I left that band when I went back to Washington and I went with Tommy Miles, see.
